slides.headline: 38% of AI citations rank in the top 10
slides.subhead: Eight months ago it was 76%. Rankings and visibility have decoupled.

slides.headline: AI decides *whether* to cite you. Not where you rank.
Being named first matters. Being named first is not stable.
slides.body: Same query, three runs, and AI Mode barely agrees with itself. Brand recognition can override position entirely.

slides.headline: Thin data about your brand means thin mentions in the answer
slides.body: Depth is a citation input, not a vanity metric. The gap between a deep page and a stub is roughly fourfold.

slides.headline: AI assigns you a tier before it describes you
slides.body: Leaders get *industry standard*. Challengers get *growing alternative*. That one word decides whether the reader acts.

slides.headline: You are not competing for position one. You are competing to own *best for X*.
slides.body: Users self-select on the category slot the model puts you in. Win the slot, not the rank.

slides.headline: Citation frequency replaces rankings as the primary metric
slides.body: Brand mention rate is the health check. Traditional rank trackers cannot see any of it.

slides.headline: Which of these four signals are you actually tracking?
slides.body: Most teams track none of them and call it an AI search strategy. Pick one this week and get a baseline.
